windows.development: decision days whose five targets fall on or before 2025-12-31 (the frame of scripts/s3c_announced_settlement_1288.py, window 'development'); decides
windows.2026: decision days whose five targets fall from 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-03 (window '2026', the near-blind tier open since GO #151); shown apart, already seen by #845, #1229, #1255, #1273, #1288 and #1321, decides nothing

unit: the cell (decision day D, lead h = 1..5), target T = the h-th panel day after D, outcome the whole-basis-point spread at T. A group of cells is read by the day type or regime of T. For a rate over all leads the series is indexed by target day: the mean of the hits of the cells that target it (up to five); for one lead it is that lead's cell series in target-day order

calibration.levels: every grid quantile (scoring_protocol.GRID, 23 levels): the share of cells with y <= q_tau ('at or below') and with y < q_tau ('strictly below'). A calibrated forecast of a whole-basis-point target has the strict share at or below tau and the at-or-below share at or above tau, so both are shown; the hit-definition question of coverage_tests is open (Eleonora's) and this study chooses neither rule
calibration.bands: the central 50% band (q25 to q75) and the central 90% band (q5 to q95): coverage with the band closed (q_lo <= y <= q_hi) and open (q_lo < y < q_hi), against 0.50 and 0.90
calibration.pit: the randomised PIT of #970 (scripts/randomised_pit_970.py: randomised_pit, the draw uniform in the cell's level bracket, ties randomised), cells drawn in (decision day, lead) order within each group; seed 1363 for the main draw, seeds 1364 to 1383 for twenty further draws. Shown: the six bins of #707 (edges 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, expected 0.10, 0.15, 0.25, 0.25, 0.15, 0.10), the share at or below 0.10 and at or above 0.90, and the range of those two shares over the twenty further seeds
calibration.interval: a 90% stationary-bootstrap percentile interval (mean block 10 target days, 2000 resamples, seed 1363) of each rate, from the series in target-day order. The current method for a day-type group (the group's target days, scattered, resampled in date order as if consecutive) is used, with the caveat that #1221 questions it and #1228 will decide; no reading of a day-type group is a finding. Groups of fewer than 20 target days are listed with their rates and not tested
calibration.reading: a group of 20 or more target days is read: for a band, 'over-covers' when the interval of coverage lies wholly above the nominal, 'under-covers' when wholly below, otherwise 'consistent'; for a grid quantile tau, 'quantile too high' when the interval of the strict share lies wholly above tau, 'quantile too low' when the interval of the at-or-below share lies wholly below tau, otherwise 'consistent'. The size is the observed rate less the nominal (for a quantile, the nearer end of [strict, at-or-below] to tau). Nothing is corrected for the number of groups and the page states the count of readings made, so that some chance flags are expected

groups.regime: the declared regimes of the splits declaration, by the regime of T (2018-19, 2020, 2021-23, 2024, 2025-26 or as declared)
groups.target_day_type: the types of T, which overlap: quarter_end, month_end, tax_date, coupon_settlement (the coupon flag of the term table), bill_settlement (the bill flag), fomc_day, iorb_window, dom_19_23, post_month_end_window (calendar_mr_1115.DAY_TYPES; 'settlement' split into its coupon and bill flags), and ordinary (none of them)
groups.pressure_day_type: the turn record in force (turn_days.reporting_day_type) of T, as every study since #1241
groups.size: every group is printed with its number of target days and cells

clustering.question: do the misses cluster in time: is the chance of a miss at lead h on decision day D+1 different after a miss on decision day D than after a hit
clustering.sequences: for each lead, window and model, the 0/1 sequence over the scored decision days in panel order (consecutive panel days; a break in the scored days starts a new run, and no transition is counted across it) of four events, each under two rules: upper tail y > q95 (strict) or y >= q95 (weak); lower tail y < q05 or y <= q05; 90% band miss, outside the closed band (strict) or outside the open band (weak); 50% band miss, likewise. Eight sequences per lead
clustering.tests: (1) Christoffersen's independence test (coverage_tests.christoffersen_independence, a first-order Markov chain against a constant probability, chi-square 1 df) on all the days, its transition counts summed over runs; (2) the same statistic's exact permutation p-value (10,000 shuffles of the sequence inside its runs, seed 1363), because the asymptotic p is weak when misses are few; (3) the protocol's own reading (scoring_protocol.coverage_cells, method 'thinned': every h-th decision day at lead h) for the q05 and q95 events; (4) the same independence test inside each regime of the development window, with no transition across a regime boundary. Descriptive: P(miss | previous miss), P(miss | previous hit), the longest run of misses, and the number of misses
clustering.reading: the permutation p of (2) is the reading. A sequence 'clusters' when its Holm-adjusted p (scoring_protocol.holm, alpha 0.05, over the family of the 40 sequences of one model and window) is below alpha; the unadjusted p is shown beside. Clustering inside a regime (4) is read the same way. These tests do not separate clustering in time from a miss rate that moves with the regime or the day type; (4) and the day-type tables are there for that
clustering.references: the same tests on B1, B1' and B2, so the candidate's clustering is read against theirs
